subject: Daypart SLO carveouts & regional resilience for hosted API
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: ops@starlightai.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Daypart SLO carveouts & regional resilience for hosted API

Hi Amina — great to connect yesterday. Per our conversation Starlight has strong diurnal traffic spikes (US mornings and APAC evenings for your customers). You asked for an approach that gives predictable p50/p95 guarantees while acknowledging short, repeatable peak windows.

Proposal (high level):
- Baseline commitments: p50 = 60ms, p95 = 220ms measured on a rolling 24h window.
- Daypart carveouts: allow a narrow scheduled peak carveout (two configurable dayparts per region, up to 90 minutes each) where p95 may be relaxed by up to 150ms provided Redwood publishes a scheduled peak window 24h in advance via the Console API.
- Transient resilience: for unplanned regional capacity pressure, automatic fallback to a compatible lower-cost model variant with p95 target relaxed up to 300ms for periods under 2 hours; incidents longer than 2 hours trigger crediting rules.
- Measurement: p50/p95 computed over user-facing request latencies at the application edge (post-redispatch, pre-response), sampled at 100% for SLO endpoints; we will provide example query and CSV export.

Next steps: I’ve attached an example CSV with the measurement query and an initial draft addendum. Can Karthik and Marissa confirm pricing/credit mechanics and we can loop Legal for contract language?

Thanks,
Jonas
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
attachments: slo-measurement-example-20270502.csv, draft-addendum-daypart-0512.pdf

From: Amina Rios <ops@starlightai.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 11:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Daypart SLO carveouts & regional resilience for hosted API

Jonas — thanks, this is helpful. A few clarifying Qs from our ops and SRE teams: 
1) Can the daypart start times be automated (we have shifting promo periods)?
2) During the daypart carveout, do you still measure p50/p95 and publish them (we need observability for our runbooks)?
3) For the fallback to a smaller model variant, is that transparent to clients (same API surface) or do we need an upgrade path in client code?

Also: we will need clear crediting language — Starlight can accept short, scheduled relaxations but wants credits when p95 exceeds committed values outside carveouts for >30 minutes. Looping in legal@starlightai.com.

—Amina
Head of Platform, Starlight AI

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Amina Rios <ops@starlightai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Daypart SLO carveouts & regional resilience for hosted API

Amina — answers inline below. Quoting your questions for clarity.

On Mon, May 3, 2027 at 11:48 AM Amina Rios <ops@starlightai.com> wrote:
> 1) Can the daypart start times be automated (we have shifting promo periods)?

Yes. We can expose a small Daypart API (or accept a CRON-ish schedule) so you can programmatically set the two dayparts per region. The Console will also show the active dayparts and allow manual overrides.

> 2) During the daypart carveout, do you still measure p50/p95 and publish them (we need observability for our runbooks)?

Yes — all measurements remain visible. Carveouts are considered in SLO evaluation (they exclude the carved minutes when computing the contracted p95) but we will publish both raw and adjusted rolling metrics so your runbooks can inspect raw degradations. Attached CSV shows the two exported series: raw_latency.csv and adjusted_latency.csv.

> 3) For the fallback to a smaller model variant, is that transparent to clients (same API surface) or do we need an upgrade path in client code?

Transparent — same API, identical schema. We’ll document behavior (e.g., slight quality differences) and add an opt-out flag if you prefer to avoid automatic fallback.

About credits: Karthik — can you confirm commercial thresholds (example below) and whether we can cap monthly credits? Proposed commercial mechanics:
- Breach credit: if p95 exceeds committed value outside scheduled carveouts for >30 continuous minutes, Starlight receives 5% service credit for the invoice period for each hour beyond the 30-minute threshold, capped at 50% for the billing period.
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance pieces <30m and agreed emergency mitigation (where both sides agree) are excluded.

If that sounds reasonable, I’ll ask Legal to draft the addendum language.

Thanks,
Jonas

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Amina Rios <ops@starlightai.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Daypart SLO carveouts & regional resilience for hosted API

Amina — quick commercial note from Redwood. We appreciate the need to limit business impact during sustained breaches; suggested adjustments: 
- Keep Jonas’ breach credit formula but allow a quarterly cap tied to committed spend (e.g., max credit = 30% of monthly invoice for customers with < $50k MRR commitment; negotiable for larger commitments).
- For scheduled dayparts, we are happy to provide one 90-minute daypart per region per week at no charge; additional dayparts or automation-triggered dayparts beyond the agreed two per region will be treated as a Premium Ops feature.

I’ve attached an example SLO export (slo-measurement-example-20270502.csv) showing how p95 is derived and the query used in our monitoring backend. Also dropping the draft addendum link — Legal can take that as a starting point: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-daypart-slo-draft

If Starlight is willing to confirm committed monthly spend band, we can present final commercial options (credit caps, premium daypart automation).

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
attachments: slo-measurement-example-20270502.csv

From: Amina Rios <ops@starlightai.com>

Thanks — this is moving in the right direction. Starlight can confirm an initial committed band of $30k/month for the pilot. We accept the proposed mechanics subject to Legal’s redlines. Two asks before we sign: 
- Please include an example of the Console API payload for creating a daypart (we want to automate schedule changes).
- Please add a short SLA paragraph that enumerates observability endpoints we can query for audit (we prefer to call the endpoints ourselves rather than receive reports).

If you can drop a short addendum draft that covers dayparts, fallback variant behavior, measurement definition (include the exact SQL/PromQL snippet), and the credit formula, we’ll get Legal to review quickly.

Amina
Head of Platform, Starlight AI
